summary: Most reviewers report poor support, constant upsells and fees that pile up, plus steep renewals and some DNS or hosting outages. Domains held for resale at high prices come up repeatedly. A fair number call it reliable and fine as a registrar, but weak for hosting and email.

Most reviewers praise low prices, solid uptime and good performance, often after leaving AWS, DigitalOcean or OVH. The main complaints are the recent price increases, which many say weaken the advantage, and support some find slow. A few had accounts blocked or deleted after failed payments or verification trouble.

Cheap for the specs, and some reviewers run it for years without trouble. Many others report outages, sometimes lasting days, slow or templated support, and slower real-world performance than advertised from overselling. Happier users tend to run side projects or non-critical services on it.

Easy to build with and fine for small sites, but many reviewers complain about unexpected renewal charges, refunds refused after cancelling, and big price rises. Support is another frequent complaint, with bots and runarounds, and some find sites slow or glitchy.

Long-time customers often call it reliable for domains, with cheap first-year prices and many TLDs. The main complaints are renewal prices that have climbed and support that is hit or miss, with some accounts or domains locked over fraud checks. Some say it is fine for domains but would not host there.

Broadly liked as a domain registrar for low, predictable renewal prices, an easy interface and simple transfers, often after leaving GoDaddy or Namecheap. The main complaint is support, which a minority find slow or unhelpful on complex issues, plus a few account lockouts. Paid email and hosting extras get less praise.

Most reviewers describe poor support, from scripted replies and agents who cannot fix problems to staff accidentally breaking live sites. Many also hit steep renewal prices, outages, slow sites, constant upsells and unexpected or hard-to-cancel charges. A few had good support or no problems.

Most reviewers find it reliable for email with a custom domain, an easy switch from Gmail or Google Workspace, and good spam filtering. Complaints include weak body-text search, occasional outages, slow support and development, and constant prompts to upgrade. A few report mail from Proton addresses landing in spam.

Reviewers are split. Many find it easy to use and stable for simple sites and small shops, but the most common complaint is support, often bots and slow replies, especially over domain renewals and failed payments after the Google Domains move. Rising prices and a few payment holds also come up.

Reviewers consistently describe it as reliable, fast and easy to use, with simple migration from Gmail or Google Workspace and strong spam filtering. Many have used it for a decade or more and say support is human and helpful. Minor complaints include a clunky calendar and limited calendar sharing outside Fastmail.

Reviewers praise how easy it is to deploy, especially Next.js, and many pay little for small or moderate sites. The main complaint is unexpected bills from traffic spikes, bots, image optimisation or edge requests, sometimes hundreds or thousands of dollars, with mixed results getting them reduced. Per-seat costs also sting small teams.

Most reviewers find it reliable, cheap and simple, often running droplets for years without problems. The main complaint is support, with new accounts auto-blocked or suspended and a few accounts and data deleted after failed payments, often with little explanation. Some are frustrated by blocked outbound email ports.

Reviewers often praise fast sites and knowledgeable support, but the most common complaint is renewal prices that jump sharply after the intro period. Some long-time customers say support has declined, with AI chat replacing humans, and a few hit inode or CPU limits.

Reviewers are split. Some, especially agencies, praise reliable hosting, strong backups and staging, and helpful support. The more common complaint is that support has declined in recent years, along with repeated upsells over traffic or bandwidth overages and a high price. Some also report slowdowns and 502 errors.

Generally praised as cheap, easy and reliable for small WordPress and client sites, with a simple panel. The main complaint is support that is mostly AI chat and hard to get past to a human, followed by renewal prices rising well above the first term. A few report suspensions or resource-limit throttling.

Reviewers split but lean positive. Many praise responsive chat support, reliability and easy server management for agencies and WordPress developers. Complaints include slow performance on small plans, especially in the WordPress admin, support that falls short on harder issues, and a markup over the underlying server price. A few had servers deleted over overdue invoices.

Most reviewers describe very reliable servers, fast hardware support and strong value. The main complaint is the recent price increases, with some saying certain models now cost several times more, plus high setup fees outside auction servers. A few had accounts cancelled over payment or verification problems, and some mention weak DDoS protection.

Reviewers overwhelmingly like it for at-cost domain pricing with no renewal markups, a clean dashboard and easy transfers, often from GoDaddy or Namecheap. The main drawback is support, which a few describe as slow or absent, along with a limited TLD list and occasional payment failures.

Reviewers praise a generous free tier, very fast static hosting and easy deploys from GitHub, often after leaving Vercel or Netlify. The frustrations are mostly with server-side frameworks, especially Next.js, where runtime limits, missing Node features and build failures sent some back to Vercel.

Admins and small teams mostly find it easy to manage and reliable, with strong spam filtering, and often prefer it to Microsoft 365. The main complaints are price increases, bundled AI features customers did not ask for, and support that is hard to reach, especially for smaller customers.

Namecheap Hosting is praised by some for cheap, no-frills cPanel hosting with friendly support, but more reviewers report poor support, slowness and outages, including a datacenter outage that took many sites and mailboxes down for hours. It suits hobby or low-stakes sites better than email-dependent businesses.

Railway is loved for being very easy to deploy to, with simple pricing that suits side projects and small production apps. The main downsides are outages and a security incident that leaked environment variables, which left some users with abused API keys, long deploy blocks and little communication from support.

Kinsta is a managed WordPress host that most reviewers praise for excellent, fast support, speed and reliability, often after moving from WP Engine. The downsides are cost and resource limits, mainly few PHP workers, paid add-ons and visit counts that include bots. Agencies running many client sites feature heavily.

Netlify is easy to use and was praised for a generous free plan, with git-push deploys that just work for static and Next.js sites. The main downsides are billing surprises, especially the credit-based pricing where frequent deploys use up the allowance, plus support that was slow or silent after account suspensions.

OVHcloud VPS is liked for stable uptime and low prices, with many users running servers for years without trouble. The main complaints are renewal price rises, older and slow CPUs on newer plans, and slow or unhelpful support, including account bans and cancellations that dragged on.

netcup is praised for strong performance and reliability at low prices, particularly its root servers, with many long-term customers happy. The main downside is slow or unhelpful support and account handling, including long verification, hard-to-cancel contracts and minimum terms. A few reported network outages.

Vultr is mostly praised for reliable, fast VPS performance and quick support, with many long-term users. The main complaint is poor support in some cases, such as suspensions, lockouts and unexplained actions, with some network problems and price increases pushing a few users to Hetzner.

Akamai Linode is praised above all for reliability, with many reviewers running servers for a decade or more, plus good support, simple pricing and an easy dashboard. Downsides are a major outage in mid 2025, a price rise after the Akamai purchase, and a few account bans at signup.

Render is easy to deploy to and praised for a free plan and predictable pricing, which suits hobby projects and small apps. The main downsides are slow free-tier spin-downs and cold starts, free-tier suspensions with little warning, and costs that add up across many services.

Hostinger VPS draws praise for easy management and a low entry price, and many users run Docker projects without trouble. The main complaints are CPU throttling and steal under load, slower performance than expected, and renewal prices that are much higher than the intro rate. Support was often described as unhelpful.

OVHcloud Bare Metal is liked for reliable dedicated servers at good prices, with several users running them for many years. The main downsides are slow or poor support, long delivery waits and cancellation trouble, with a few outages and slow hardware on cheaper ranges.

Zoho Mail is mostly praised as cheap, trouble-free custom-domain email, with a useful free plan and smooth moves from Google or GoDaddy. A few found setup and account management complicated, and some mentioned weak spam filtering or occasional IMAP hiccups.

RackNerd is a budget VPS provider that most reviewers find very good value, with long stretches of reliable uptime for small personal projects and mail servers. Downsides are a few cases of slow speeds, outages and unhelpful support, plus no built-in backups or firewall.

Hetzner Server Auction is loved for dedicated servers at very low prices compared with cloud providers, and long-term users report few problems apart from occasional drive failures. The main downside is price increases on existing servers, though most found the recent adjustment small.

DreamHost is mostly praised for reliable shared and VPS hosting with helpful support, and many users have stayed for years. Downsides are few: some slowness on managed WordPress plans, a long outage for one customer, and price rises on VPS.

Most reviewers find IONOS VPS very cheap and stable, with several reporting years of use without problems. The main downsides are price increases, hard-to-cancel contracts and some reports of overprovisioned, slow hosts. It suits small or throwaway projects well.

Most reviewers, many of them long-time customers from the A2 Hosting days, praise its helpful support and steady uptime. Complaints centre on renewal price increases and support that has become more AI-driven since the takeover, with a few reporting outages or slow patching.

Reviews are mostly about its domain registrar side, where most reviewers find it cheap, simple and trouble-free, including bulk transfers from other registrars. Several report quick, friendly refunds. A few had bad experiences with domain handling and support, and one finds the dashboard weak.

Experiences split sharply. Several long-time users find it dependable and keep it for years, while a larger group reports poor support, billing errors or charges they never ordered, and some outages. Those who stay tend to be happy; those who hit billing problems struggle to resolve them.

Most reviewers find Fly.io easy to deploy to and cheap, with several running small apps on the free allowance without trouble. The main downsides are past outages and a more hands-on setup for databases and linked services. It suits small apps and developers comfortable with the terminal.

Most reviewers have used NameSilo for years without problems and like its pricing and free WHOIS privacy. Complaints are mixed: poor support, renewal price rises, higher costs without funds on deposit, and a dated interface. It suits people who want a no-frills registrar.

Opinion is split, but the main complaint is poor support, with several long-time customers saying it declined over the years. Others report price rises, upselling and a few outages. Some customers have had stable hosting for years and found support helpful.

Most reviewers find InMotion reliable with helpful, easy-to-reach support, and some move up to its VPS as sites grow. Downsides are a recent decline in support access for one long-time customer and a steep renewal increase for another.

Most reviewers run small servers on its generous free tier and report stable, trouble-free use, some for years. The main risk is that free instances can be hard to obtain, flagged idle or removed without warning. It suits hobby projects, not anything critical.

Most reviewers, including several long-term customers, praise its support and easy dashboard for WordPress sites, with backups and staging included. Downsides are fewer features than WP Engine, and one report of slower speeds after the acquisition. It suits agencies and freelancers managing client sites.

Most reviewers praise its fast load times and support that connects them to a real person quickly. Several switched from WP Engine, Kinsta or Bluehost and stayed. Downsides are a higher cost and one report that it struggled with a heavier plugin-based site.

Reviewers consistently like Dynadot as a registrar: simple interface, fair pricing, no upselling and easy transfers. Several have kept domains there for years. No clear downsides appeared in the reviews.

Most reviewers are long-time customers who left or are leaving over domain renewal prices that rose sharply after the company changed hands. Some also dislike mailboxes becoming a paid extra. Those who stayed still credit the reliable service and clean tools.

Most reviewers find Pressable rock solid for WordPress, with several running client or WooCommerce sites there for years and moving over from WP Engine or Kinsta. Support is described as supportive. One reviewer found it poor, citing unsupported plugins and paid upgrades.
